relations.myth: Creation of the good material Earth
relations.note: Mazda creates or establishes Earth; the Bundahišn later expands the cosmogony.
Ārmaiti is Earth's divine guardian or spiritual patron, but remains distinct from Zam.
Ahriman invades and makes Earth tremble; rising mountains stabilize her.
Later priestly classification places Zamyād among Amurdad's divine helpers.
Rashn appears beside Zamyād in later divine catalogues and blessing traditions.
relations.source: Greater Bundahišn; Āfrīn ī Haft Aməšaspand

relations.note: Aštād appears beside Zamyād in later divine catalogues and blessing traditions.
relations.source: Greater Bundahišn; Āfrīn ī Haft Aməšaspand

relations.myth: Calendrical association of Earth and Glory
relations.note: Zamyād and the Glories share later calendrical and priestly groupings without narrative interaction.

relations.myth: Worship of sustaining Earth and waters
relations.note: Earth and the life-bearing waters are juxtaposed and worshipped in the same liturgy.
